title: Cognitive efficiency in VR simulated natural indoor environments examined through EEG and affective responses

findings.antecedent: Wooden interior (W) environment vs control condition (C) - virtual reality simulated indoor environments with natural design elements
findings.statement: The wooden interior (W) condition showed significantly higher ATR in the frontal region compared to the control condition, reflecting greater alpha activity and enhanced attentional engagement.

instruments_used.name: Electroencephalography (EEG)
instruments_used.construct_measured: Alpha-to-theta ratio in frontal region (AF3, F7, E3, F4, F8, AH)

findings.source: Results section, Table 1, Alpha-to-theta ratio (ATR) findings
findings.quote: A significant main effect of condition was observed, (F(3, 105) = 4.27, p = 0.007, η²p = 0.109), indicating that ATR in the frontal region significantly varied across the conditions.

scope_conditions.setting: Virtual reality laboratory environment at Yonsei University

stimulus_description.primary_type: Virtual reality simulated indoor environments (wooden interior lounge)
stimulus_description.components: Wooden furniture, natural materials, wood finishes, realistic lounge setting

findings.mechanism: Higher ATR reflects a balance between alpha activity (associated with relaxation and internal focus) and theta activity (associated with cognitive load), suggesting enhanced attentional engagement and relaxation.
moderators_reported: Environmental design elements (curvilinear forms vs straight forms)

source_quality_indicators.replication_status: first empirical test of this specific design comparison

findings.antecedent: Wooden interior (W) condition - natural design element exposure
findings.statement: The W condition exhibited significantly lower TBR compared to control, indicating reduced cognitive load and enhanced attentional focus with sustained attention.
findings.quote: Theta-to-beta ratio (TBR): A significant main effect of condition was found, (F(3, 105) = 4.19, p = 0.008, η²p = 0.107), reflecting a moderate effect size, indicating a meaningful impact of the experimental environments.

stimulus_description.primary_type: Virtual reality simulated indoor environments (wooden interior lounge)
stimulus_description.components: Wooden furniture, natural materials, wood finishes

findings.mechanism: Lower theta-to-beta ratio indicates reduced theta activity relative to beta activity, suggesting decreased cognitive load and increased external attention focus, supporting enhanced cognitive engagement.

findings.antecedent: Wooden interior (W) condition vs other conditions (C, CL, N)
findings.statement: The W condition showed significantly higher ABR compared to control, indicating greater alpha power and a more relaxed neurophysiological state with enhanced visual comfort.

instruments_used.name: Electroencephalography (EEG)
instruments_used.construct_measured: Alpha-to-beta ratio in occipital region (O1, O2)

findings.quote: Analysis revealed a significant main effect of condition, F(3, 105) = 5.56, p = 0.001, η²p = 0.137, indicating substantial differences in ABR across conditions.

stimulus_description.primary_type: Virtual reality simulated indoor environments with natural design elements
stimulus_description.components: Wooden interior with natural materials and design

findings.mechanism: Higher ABR reflects increased alpha activity, indicating a relaxed neurophysiological state. This is associated with reduced cognitive strain and enhanced visual comfort, suggesting the wooden interior fosters a calmer visual processing state.

findings.antecedent: Wooden interior (W) condition compared to curvilinear forms (CL) condition
findings.statement: Participants in the W condition reported significantly higher relaxation compared to the CL condition, with the W condition showing the strongest relaxation effects.

instruments_used.name: Self-reported affective response scales
instruments_used.construct_measured: Relaxation and valence ratings on semantic differential scales

findings.quote: The CL condition demonstrated the largest difference, t(35) = 4.246, SE = 0.292, p < 0.001, when compared to the control condition.

stimulus_description.delivery_method: VR headset display with self-report questionnaire
stimulus_description.components: Wooden lounge interior with natural materials

findings.mechanism: Wooden design elements appear to create atmospheres conducive to relaxation through their natural material properties and warm aesthetic qualities.

findings.antecedent: Wooden interior (W) condition vs control condition (C)
findings.statement: The W condition elicited significantly higher positive emotions compared to control, with participants reporting higher positive valence and emotional engagement.
findings.quote: A significant main effect of condition was observed for relaxation (F(3, 105) = 7.94, p < 0.001, η²p = 0.185) and valence (F(3, 105) = 20, p < 0.001, η²p = 0.388), indicating substantial differences in affective responses across the conditions.

stimulus_description.delivery_method: VR headset (Meta Quest 2) with post-viewing questionnaire
stimulus_description.components: Wooden interior with natural materials, warm aesthetic

findings.mechanism: Natural design elements (particularly wood) elicit positive emotional responses through their biophilic properties and aesthetic appeal, supporting psychological well-being.

findings.antecedent: Wooden interior (W) condition compared to all other conditions (C, CL, N)
findings.consequent: Cognitive task performance (composite score across Error Detection, Stroop, and Go/No-Go tasks)
findings.statement: Participants in the W condition achieved significantly higher cognitive performance scores compared to control and other natural design conditions, indicating superior cognitive efficiency.

instruments_used.name: Error Detection Task
instruments_used.construct_measured: Accuracy in identifying spelling errors in passage reading

instruments_used.name: Stroop Test
instruments_used.construct_measured: Selective attention and cognitive flexibility (color-word interference)

findings.source: Results section, Cognitive performance findings, Table 1
findings.quote: A repeated measure ANOVA revealed a significant main effect of condition on cognitive performance (F(3, 105) = 31.6, p < 0.001, η²p = 0.475), indicating substantial differences across the conditions.

scope_conditions.measurement_type: Cognitive task battery (reaction time, accuracy, error detection)

stimulus_description.primary_type: Virtual interior environments followed by cognitive task execution
stimulus_description.delivery_method: VR headset for environment, virtual keyboard for task responses
stimulus_description.components: VR-simulated lounge with varying design elements (control, curvilinear forms, nature views, wooden interior)

findings.mechanism: The wooden interior environment supports a relaxed yet attentive mental state, characterized by high alpha activity relative to theta activity and positive affect, which together optimize cognitive task performance through balanced emotional and neurological states.
moderators_reported: Environmental design elements (wood, natural views, curvilinear forms)

source_quality_indicators.replication_status: first comprehensive test of natural design on cognition

findings.antecedent: Nature view (N) condition vs control and other conditions
findings.statement: The nature view (N) condition did not produce significant differences in cognitive performance compared to control, suggesting that viewing natural scenes alone through a window-like interface is insufficient to enhance cognitive function without sustained immersive exposure.
findings.quote: In contrast, no significant differences emerged among the CL, N, and W conditions, indicating comparable cognitive performance across these groups.

stimulus_description.primary_type: Virtual reality window view showing nature scenery with trees and flowers
stimulus_description.components: Virtual landscape with diverse trees, flowers, visible through window

findings.mechanism: Nature views through limited visual exposure may provide emotional benefits but fail to engage the immersive, multisensory engagement required for sustained cognitive enhancement. Visual complexity without spatial immersion may actually increase cognitive load rather than support focus.

findings.statement: The curvilinear forms condition did not significantly improve cognitive performance compared to control, suggesting that curved architectural elements alone are insufficient to enhance task performance without additional natural design features.
findings.quote: In contrast, no significant differences emerged among the CL, N, and W conditions, indicating comparable cognitive performance across these groups.

stimulus_description.primary_type: Virtual interior with curvilinear architectural forms
stimulus_description.components: Curved walls, rounded furniture, curved ceiling elements

findings.mechanism: While curved forms are intended to introduce biophilic elements through organic shapes, their impact without material authenticity (such as wood) or spatial complexity (like nature views) is minimal for cognitive enhancement.

findings.antecedent: Regression model predicting cognitive task performance from neurophysiological and affective factors
findings.consequent: Alpha-to-theta ratio (ATR) as predictor of cognitive performance
findings.statement: ATR demonstrated a significant positive effect on cognitive performance (β = 0.206, p = 0.01), indicating that higher alpha-to-theta ratio predicts better cognitive task performance across all environmental conditions.

instruments_used.name: EEG-derived neurophysiological measure
instruments_used.construct_measured: Alpha-to-theta ratio from EEG frontal electrodes

findings.source: Results section, Effects of neurophysiological and affective responses on cognitive performance, Table 2
findings.quote: Among the neurophysiological predictors, the ATR had a significant positive effect on cognitive performance, (β = 0.206, p = 0.01), indicating that higher ATR levels were associated with improved performance.

scope_conditions.measurement_type: Multiple regression analysis across all conditions

stimulus_description.primary_type: Across all four VR experimental conditions
stimulus_description.components: Control, curvilinear forms, nature views, wooden interior

findings.mechanism: Higher alpha-to-theta ratio reflects a balanced neural state favoring internal focus and relaxation (alpha) over cognitive load (theta), which supports efficient task execution through reduced mental fatigue.

findings.antecedent: Regression model with relaxation as predictor
findings.statement: Relaxation was a significant predictor of cognitive performance (β = 0.173, p = 0.041), indicating that higher self-reported relaxation was associated with better cognitive task outcomes.

instruments_used.name: Affective self-report scale
instruments_used.construct_measured: Self-reported relaxation level on Likert scale

findings.source: Results section, Effects of neurophysiological and affective responses, Table 2
findings.quote: Among the affective responses, the relaxation was also a significant predictor (β = 0.173, p = 0.041), suggesting that higher relaxation levels contributed to enhanced cognitive task outcomes.
findings.mechanism: Relaxation may support cognitive performance through reduced physiological arousal and mental fatigue, allowing greater attentional resources to be allocated to task execution.

findings.consequent: Environmental factor effect on cognitive performance (regression model)
findings.statement: Only the W condition showed a significant positive effect on cognitive performance in the regression model (β = 0.353, p = 0.002), confirming that wooden interior environments uniquely enhance cognitive outcomes compared to other design conditions.

instruments_used.name: Cognitive task battery composite score
instruments_used.construct_measured: Across Error Detection, Stroop, and Go/No-Go tasks

findings.quote: Regarding environmental conditions, only the W condition showed a significant positive effect (β = 0.353, p = 0.002), indicating that cognitive performance was notably higher in this environment compared to the reference category (C condition).

stimulus_description.components: Wooden furniture, natural wood materials, warm wood finishes

findings.mechanism: The wooden interior creates an optimal psychophysiological state through combined effects: relaxation from natural materials, attentional restoration from aesthetic properties, and reduced cognitive load from spatial coherence, all supporting cognitive task performance.

findings.antecedent: Curvilinear forms (CL) and Nature views (N) conditions
findings.statement: Neither the curvilinear forms condition (β = 0.013, p = 0.374) nor the nature views condition (β = 0.017, p = 0.314) showed significant effects on cognitive performance in the regression model, indicating these design approaches alone are insufficient to enhance task performance.
findings.source: Results section, Table 2 regression model results
findings.quote: However, CL (β = 0.013, p = 0.374) and N (β = 0.017, p = 0.314) were not statistically significant, suggesting that these environmental conditions did not have a substantial impact on cognitive performance.

stimulus_description.primary_type: VR environments with curvilinear forms and nature views
stimulus_description.components: Curved architectural elements; nature scenery viewed through window

findings.mechanism: These design approaches may support emotional well-being but lack the integrated sensory and material properties necessary for sustained cognitive enhancement. Curved forms alone and visual nature exposure without immersion do not create the optimal psychophysiological conditions for task performance.

findings.antecedent: Overall regression model of neurophysiological, affective, and environmental predictors
findings.statement: The combined regression model including neurophysiological responses (ATR), affective responses (relaxation), and environmental factors (W condition) explained 14.8% of variance in cognitive task performance (R² = 0.148, adjusted R² = 0.117, F(5,138) = 4.774, p < 0.001), indicating a moderate and statistically significant predictive effect.

instruments_used.name: Multiple regression model
instruments_used.construct_measured: Combined effects of EEG, affective responses, and environmental factors on task performance

findings.source: Results section, Effects of neurophysiological and affective responses on cognitive performance
findings.quote: The final model was statistically significant, F(5,138) = 4.774, p < 0.001, explaining approximately 14.8% of the variance in cognitive task performance (R² = 0.148, adjusted R² = 0.117).

scope_conditions.setting: Virtual reality laboratory at Yonsei University
scope_conditions.population: Korean undergraduate and graduate students, N=36
scope_conditions.measurement_type: Multiple predictors: EEG (ATR), self-report (relaxation), environmental condition (W/CL/N/C)

stimulus_description.delivery_method: Meta Quest 2 VR headset with simultaneous EEG recording
stimulus_description.components: Control (neutral office), Curvilinear forms (curved furniture), Nature views (window scenery), Wooden interior (natural materials)

findings.mechanism: A synergistic relationship among neurophysiological balance (ATR), emotional regulation (relaxation), and environmental design (wood) collectively support cognitive efficiency. This multimodal predictive model suggests that cognitive enhancement requires coordinated effects across neural, affective, and environmental domains.
moderators_reported: Environmental design (wood, curvilinear forms, nature views)

findings.antecedent: Wooden interior condition - higher alpha activity and positive affect
findings.consequent: Mental state characterized as relaxed yet attentive
findings.statement: The W condition produced a distinctive psychophysiological state combining elevated ATR (alpha dominance) with positive affect, creating what the authors characterize as alert relaxation - a balance between internal calm and external attention that optimizes task performance.
findings.quote: The elevated ATR observed in the W condition suggests a potential mental state involving both internal tranquility and outward attentional readiness. This pattern potentially supports cognitive engagement without requiring deliberate cognitive effort.

scope_conditions.measurement_type: EEG + post-VR self-report + cognitive task performance

stimulus_description.delivery_method: VR headset with simultaneous EEG monitoring
stimulus_description.components: Natural wood materials, warm aesthetic, realistic lounge furniture

findings.mechanism: Wood's natural material properties, warm color temperature, and organic forms combine to reduce arousal while maintaining attentional focus. This creates a neurophysiological state (high alpha, low theta) and emotional state (relaxed, positively valenced) that together optimize cognitive task execution.

findings.antecedent: Nature view (N) condition - complex visual scene with diverse vegetation
findings.consequent: Reduced cognitive performance relative to W condition, despite emotional engagement
findings.statement: The N condition elicited positive emotions but failed to support cognitive task performance, suggesting that visual complexity without spatial immersion and material authenticity creates competing attentional demands that interfere with task focus.
findings.quote: The unexpected lower cognitive performance in the N condition, which contradicted the initial hypothesis... visual complexity of the N condition appears to have captured participants' attention toward external stimuli, potentially compromising the internal cognitive processes essential for optimal task performance.

scope_conditions.duration: 3 minutes VR viewing + 3 minutes cognitive tasks

stimulus_description.primary_type: Virtual reality window view of nature scenery
stimulus_description.components: Diverse vegetation (trees, flowers), realistic landscape, visible through window frame

findings.mechanism: While nature exposure typically provides emotional restoration benefits (positive affect, relaxation), the visual richness and spatial depth of the complex natural scene may draw attention away from task demands. Without the spatial anchoring of immersive architecture or the material simplicity of wood elements, the nature view creates external attentional pull that competes with task-focused attention.

limitations: Sample comprised only Korean college students, limiting generalizability to broader populations, particularly across cultural and demographic contexts

VR-based experimental setup, while allowing precise environmental control, may not fully capture the multisensory complexity of real-world indoor environments (tactile sensations, ambient temperature, olfactory cues)
Study design included only Korean college students in a minimally furnished space, limiting ecological validity regarding real-world architecture applications
Wooden interior condition intentionally maximized wood coverage to enhance detectability of effects, potentially overrepresenting wood's impact compared to typical architectural applications
Visual extent of natural elements was not systematically quantified across conditions, limiting ability to compare visual proportions
Single, minimally furnished space design may not generalize across diverse spatial typologies and architectural scales
Study reflects characteristics of real-world architecture but VR-based nature of stimuli may not fully capture ecological validity of real physical environments

overall_theory_links.relevance: Predicts that natural and nature-inspired environments restore attentional capacity. Study findings support this, particularly for wooden interiors.
Posits that natural environments promote physiological recovery and stress reduction. Study demonstrates increased relaxation and balanced neural activity in W condition.
Proposes inherent human affinity for natural forms and materials. Study findings support positive emotional responses to wooden interiors.

key_hypotheses_tested.statement: Nature-integrated indoor environments will induce neural activity patterns associated with a relaxed and attentive mental state compared to a neutral indoor environment without natural elements
key_hypotheses_tested.evidence: W condition showed significantly higher ATR and lower TBR, indicating enhanced alpha activity (relaxation marker) and reduced theta activity (cognitive load marker)

key_hypotheses_tested.statement: Participants in nature-integrated indoor environments will report greater positive emotions and relaxation than those in the control condition
key_hypotheses_tested.evidence: W condition elicited significantly higher relaxation (p < 0.001) and positive valence (p < 0.001) compared to control

key_hypotheses_tested.statement: Cognitive performance will be higher in nature-integrated indoor environments compared to the control condition
key_hypotheses_tested.evidence: W condition showed significantly higher cognitive task performance (F(3,105) = 31.6, p < 0.001, η²p = 0.475)

key_hypotheses_tested.statement: Neurophysiological patterns associated with relaxation and attentiveness, along with positive affective responses, will correlate with higher cognitive performance
key_hypotheses_tested.evidence: Regression model confirmed ATR (β = 0.206, p = 0.01) and relaxation (β = 0.173, p = 0.041) as significant cognitive performance predictors

design_features.study_design: Within-subject experimental design with repeated measures
condition_names: Nature views (N) - window view of natural scenery
Wooden interior (W) - natural wood materials and finishes
design_features.randomization: Participants randomly assigned to different sequences of experimental conditions (6 different sequences) to control for order effects
design_features.blinding_status: Participants were blind to experimental hypotheses; experimenters were not blind to conditions

cognitive_performance_measures: Error Detection Task (accuracy and response time)
Go/No-Go Test (reaction time, error rate, normalized)

statistical_details.anova_approach: Repeated measures ANOVA with Greenhouse-Geisser correction for sphericity violations
statistical_details.regression_approach: Multiple regression with environment as dummy-coded categorical variable (reference: control condition)
statistical_details.multicollinearity_check: Variance Inflation Factor (VIF) values all below 3 (ATR = 2.72, ABR = 2.45, TBR = 2.06)
statistical_details.effect_size_interpretation: Small: η²p < 0.01; Medium: η²p 0.06-0.14; Large: η²p > 0.14
